title: Ordinary Kunneth at a finite coefficient ring
statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraically closed field of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and let $X,Y$ be
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, for $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\geq1$, and $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$.
Use the ordinary unbounded small etale derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the canonical Kunneth arrow of [def-kun-kunneth-map].
For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and
$L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ in the
derived categories,
write $K\boxtimes_A^L L=p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$, using the
derived tensor product.
The exterior-product map is an isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma(Y,L)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).
$$

proof.text: The coefficient quotient is finite by Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing. The spectral norm of l is less than one, hence l lies in the recorded maximal ideal (uniformizer). Thus l^n is zero in the nth uniformizer quotient. Since l differs from the characteristic of k, l^n is a unit on Spec k. This supplies HasInvertibleExponent for the actual finite coefficient ring, without changing coefficients.

The fixed algebraic closure is separably closed. Apply the existing arbitrary-finite-ring theorem isIso_kunnethMap_of_isSepClosed to the product square. Finite type is LocallyOfFiniteType plus QuasiCompact; no residue-field reduction or boundedness assumption is required.

Use the canonical-map equality of lem-pur-absolute-kunneth-comparison. The constants functor on the separably closed point is an equivalence, hence its derived adjunction unit, counit and tensor comparison are isomorphisms. Expanding the point tensor mate by the adjunction unit formula expresses the transported relative arrow as a composite of isomorphisms, so the given absolute arrow is invertible. The chosen normalized constant-presheaf monoidal core agrees with the standard identity-component core: compare their unit and tensor components, then compose with monoidal sheafification.
